key_insight: Interfacial lattice distortion in HoFeO3–BaTiO3 nanofibers is consistent with stabilized ferroelectric domains and enhanced hybrid mechanical-energy harvesting.
engineering_relevance: Lead-free oxide heterostructures offer a route to improve energy-harvester output through interface engineering rather than polymer-dominated designs.
method: Fabricate HoFeO3–BaTiO3 heterostructures by alternating sol–gel electrospinning.
Probe lattice distortion and polarization using XRD refinement, HRTEM, Raman spectroscopy, and electrical measurements.
Encapsulate nanofibers in PDMS and evaluate hybrid piezoelectric–triboelectric output under cyclic impact.
evidence_signal: The heterostructure delivered 24.31 µW/cm³ at a 4.7 MΩ load—2.4× the BaTiO3 control and 8.7× the HoFeO3 control—with open-circuit peaks near +6 V and −8 V.
watch_item: The hybrid output does not isolate the piezoelectric and triboelectric contributions, limiting attribution of the gain solely to strain-stabilized domains.
paper_title: Stabilization of Ferroelectric Domains via Interfacial Strain in HoFeO3- BaTiO3 Nanofiber Heterostructures for Enhanced Hybrid Energy Harvesting
